CONVENTIONS.thermal: delta = 1-s, x = Delta_sigma = delta/2, t = sqrt(x), Delta_eps = 1 + sum_n C_n t^n
CONVENTIONS.invariants: T(delta) = delta/2 + T2 delta^2 + T3 delta^3 + ..., D(delta) = -2 delta + D2 delta^2 + D3 delta^3 + D4 delta^4 + ...; Delta_pm = 1 + T/2 pm sqrt(T^2/4 - D), Delta_eps = Delta_-
CONVENTIONS.cutoff: eps = dimensionless hard core on CONSECUTIVE kink gaps only; l = log(eps); unit interval; kappa = 1
CONVENTIONS.zeta_symbols: z2..z6 = zeta(2)..zeta(6); L2 = log 2; L3 = log 3; Li2h = Li2(-1/2); Li4h = Li4(1/2)

DEFINITIONS.f_delta: f_delta(r) = (r^delta - 1)/delta  (kappa=1), f_0 = log r;  d^j f/d delta^j at 0 = log^(j+1)(r)/(j+1)
DEFINITIONS.charges: q_i = (-1)^(i+1), i = 1..n (alternating, first kink +1); q_i q_j = (-1)^(i+j)
DEFINITIONS.domain: Omega_n(eps) = {0 < X_1 < ... < X_n < 1 : X_{i+1} - X_i >= eps}; NO wall-endpoint core
DEFINITIONS.kernel: W_n(v,delta;X) = exp[ 2 v sum_{i<j} q_i q_j f_delta(X_j - X_i) ];  at (1,0): W_n = prod_{i<j} (X_j-X_i)^(2 q_i q_j)

raw_moments.A_1: 1 (external normalization), its source derivative E A_1 = j_1 = int_0^1 [f(X)+f(1-X)] dX = -2/(1+delta) (v-independent)
raw_moments.E M_n: first endpoint-source derivative at eta=0: integrand multiplied by e(delta) = sum_i q_i [f_delta(X_i) +/- f_delta(1-X_i)] (+ for odd n = U^odd, - for even n = U^even); after integration identical to the reflected form e(delta) = 2 sum_i q_i f_delta(X_i) (reflection X -> 1-X maps Omega_n to itself, preserves W_n and D_{2m}, and q_{n+1-i} = -q_i (n even) / +q_i (n odd)). Reflection is NOT valid for second source derivatives (note l.283); none are needed for C6/C7.
raw_moments.E derivative pieces (reflected): e0 = 2 sum q_i log X_i ; e1 = d_delta e = sum q_i log^2 X_i ; e2 = d_delta^2 e = (2/3) sum q_i log^3 X_i  (at delta=0). Unreflected: e0 = sum q_i[log X_i +/- log(1-X_i)], e1 = (1/2) sum q_i[log^2 X_i +/- log^2(1-X_i)], e2 = (1/3) sum q_i[log^3 X_i +/- log^3(1-X_i)]
raw_moments.S_j: S_j = sum_{i<k} q_i q_k log^j(X_k - X_i)
raw_moments.derivative_naming: atom M_<der>: der in base,v,vv,vvv,d,vd,vvd,dd,vdd = full partial derivative d_v^a d_delta^b (NOT Taylor coefficient) at (v,delta)=(1,0), taken on the integrand (also acting on the endpoint factor e(delta) for E moments) BEFORE the eps expansion
raw_moments.eps_expansion: each raw atom is a finite-cutoff function M(eps) = sum_{p>=pmin} sum_{k>=0} c_{p,k} eps^p l^k; positive powers p>0 are genuine and must be kept
raw_moments.coordinate_reductions (optional, value-p: non-E moments: integrate the first position -> translation factor (1 - span), X_j = j*eps + T_j, 0<T_1<..<T_{n-1}<1-(n-1)eps; E moments keep all n absolute positions X_j = (j-1) eps + T_j

RAW_MOMENT_REQUIREMENTS.summary: Tight (minimal) set: 75 raw atoms (2..8 kinks), 195 scalars [eps^p l^k] with p in {-2..2}, k in {0,1}. Safe set: 204 scalars (+9: 6 below the tight bound, which must vanish, and 3 genuine positive-power coefficients that multiply them). Only l^0 and l^1 of a raw coefficient can reach [eps^0 l^0], [eps^0 l^1] of a product; a raw moment entering linearly needs only l^m. 56 of the tight scalars belong to Z2_*/Q2_* and are known exactly (out/two_kink_exact.json). For the higher-log validation targets the same eps windows are needed with the full log polynomial.
RAW_MOMENT_REQUIREMENTS.tight_bounds_argument: Power counting of the hard-core collapse (eps -> 0). The leading eps^-j comes from j pairs collapsed to gaps O(eps), each pair contributing O(1/eps) through its r^-2 kernel. A_{2m+1}, Z_{2m}: all m pairs collapse -> eps^-m (the lone charge of A, the endpoint factor of EA are O(1)). Q_{2m}: the dipole D_{2m} is O(eps) when all pairs collapse, O(1) when one pair is open -> eps^-(m-1). EZ_{2m}: the reflected endpoint factor 2 sum q_i log X_i is O(eps/X) per collapsed pair -> eps^-(m-1). EQ_{2m}: dipole and endpoint factors each cost one power when all pairs collapse, both are O(1) with one pair open -> eps^-(m-1) for m >= 2 and eps^0 for EQ2. The safe bound -floor(n/2) (Q2: 0) does not use this; the assembler checks the difference.
RAW_MOMENT_REQUIREMENTS.safe_bounds: pmin=-floor(n/2) for every raw moment except Q2 (0); Z2 support {-1,0}, Q2 support {0,1}
RAW_MOMENT_REQUIREMENTS.policy: Integration teams supply every TIGHT scalar plus the below-bound scalars (they must come out zero within precision). scripts/assemble_from_raw.py --windows both (the default) refuses missing scalars, asserts the below-bound ones vanish (--zero-tol) and requires the tight and safe assemblies to agree (--agree-tol). The genuine positive-power extras are looked up only if their partner is non-zero (a convention error), in which case a missing one is an error.

structural_zeros.top_log: for a jet d_v^i d_delta^j of a normalized response of order n (C_n, K_n), [eps^0 l^k] = 0 for k > n - 1 + i + 2j; checked by the RG formulas (the predicted [l^(top+1)] vanishes identically) and on the phase-2 data

pole_cancellation.statement: every [eps^p l^k], p < 0, of every normalized jet vanishes; the raw windows needed for the new jets are poles_C8.json -> raw_needed_for_new_jets (all log powers)

structural_zeros.below_tight_bound: the 12 safe-minus-tight scalars below the tight bound (raw_requirements_C8.json -> safe_minus_tight) vanish

C9, d_delta C7, d_v K8, d_v^2 K6, d_v d_delta K6, d_delta^2 C5) the coefficients [eps^0 l^k], k = 2 .. top+1, are predicted from lower-order data (normalized C, K and E jets at log powers < k) and the beta inputs
data_dependent_RG.l0_identity: the [l^0] part of the same identity reproduces the recurrence for all 35 inputs (rg_logs_C8.json -> l0_identity_equals_recurrence), including lambda6, j7 and b9

every C8-era decimal of the note Secs. 16-17 and of the archive records (comparison_C8/archive_C8_values.json)

AMBIGUITIES_AND_DISCREPANCIES.issue: d_delta acts on the endpoint factor as well as on the kernel (note l.421 "Tail derivatives also act on endpoint factors").
AMBIGUITIES_AND_DISCREPANCIES.resolution: raw_atoms integrands: sum_j binom(b,j) e_j * insertion(a,b-j)

AMBIGUITIES_AND_DISCREPANCIES.issue: Only first source derivatives are needed (j7 = -2 d_v C7_0 + (E C7)_0, lambda6 with E K6); the reflected form is valid for all of them, with any d_v, d_delta.

The CS identity and the trace algebra use b3(1,0) = 1 (F = z + u + ...), which the input expansions write as C3_1[v0d0] - 4; they agree because C3_1[v0d0] = 5 (note l.550). Data that violate it give inputs and invariants on different footings (the framework then differs from the spec assembler).
AMBIGUITIES_AND_DISCREPANCIES.resolution: the C8 assembler rejects data with |C3_1[v0d0] - 5| > agree-tol
